content: Plague is a severe and potentially fatal infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. This disease occurs naturally in certain regions of the western United States, where it is maintained in populations of wild rodents and other animals. Humans typically contract plague through the bite of a flea that has fed on an infected rodent or by coming into direct contact with an infected animal. Plague is treatable with antibiotics, but it is critical that treatment is initiated promptly to avoid severe complications or death. Historically, plague is notorious for causing widespread devastation, including the deaths of millions of people in Europe during the Middle Ages. In modern times, plague is rare but continues to persist as a cause of illness in rural areas of the western United States, as well as in certain parts of Africa and Asia.
